Perilous Realms uses an account system to allow users to play the game
using only one login.  This method ensures an easy way to keep track of 
all of your characters, and keep up to date with all changes in the game.

Please note:
Each user is allowed ONE account, owning more than one account falls into
the category of multiplaying.  Please see the helpfiles regarding laws and
multiplaying for more detailed information on the subject.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------  

In the past, Perilous Realms was supported by donations.  Based on these
donations, there were some in game incentives for supporting the game.

Using the command "account" in game would show you the amount of funds you 
have donated to the game.

Currently, there are no in game incentives for donations toward the
operation of Perilous Realms.  Supporting Perilous Realms today includes, 
playing, enjoying, and encouraging others to join, is viewed as the best 
means of support one could offer.

In the rare instance you may find yourself with an account problem, please speak
to an immortal who is a "God" or higher.  These immortals are able to access
aspects of your account to help you, should you ever need help in this regard.

If your account problem has to do with your password settings, please contact
an implementor.  It is the policy of Perilous Realms that we don't accept
notes or mudmails with requests to change passwords.  You need to be online and
make yourself available to explain what specifically is going on.  At times
an implementor's time can be very limited, so please be as forth comming and
as specific as you can.  Doing so will speed up the process.

Armor Class (AC) is the scale used to describe how well you are protected from physical
attacks.  The lower the Armor Class, the higher your chance of avoiding being hit.
In addition to Armor Class, each particular piece of armor has a certain amount of
"stopping power".  Armor Class will reflect how hard it is to hit you, while stop-
ping power will reflect how much damage is negated (or stopped) from being inflicted on 
your character.

In Perilous Realms, there exist many different type of armors.  Some high quality that
looks as if made by the gods themselfs, while other types of equipment may look as if
it was made by a five year old child out of flowers and candy wrapers.

Attributes shows you some statistics about your character.  This is 
information that is important to you know about your character, as 
it has direct relation to your character's abilities.

A brief overview of how these attributes affect your character is as follows:

STR - Strength
Strength represents your character's physical power.  This power is reflected
by how much a character can carry, how hard a character can hit something,
and in conjunction with dexterity determines endurance (also known as moves).
The maximum strength any character can achieve is 30 points.

Int - Intelligence
Intelligence influences how quickly someone can learn information.  As such
it directly affects how much casting power a mage type character will earn.
In addition to that, intelligence affects how effectively your character
can think on his feet and chose to move out of the way when a fist or mace
is being swung at its head.  The maximum intelligence any character can
achieve is 25 points.

Wis - Wisdom
Wisdom is the proper application of knowledge.  Like intelligence it will effect
ones ability to earn mana, which is important for clerical type classes.  When
combined with a high intelligence it allows you to get a better understanding
of trainings, thus affecting practice sessions gained per each level.  The maxi-
mum wisdom any character can achieve is 25 points.

Dex - Dexterity
Dexterity is the description of how nimble a character is.  The more nimble you
are, the faster you can move out of the way of a strike and thus avoid wounds.
Ones dexterity will effect how quickly and how accurately you hit a foe.
This also effects how "light" you feel on your feet, and effects you endurance.
The maximum dexterity any character can achieve is 25 points.

Con - Constitution
Constitution is the description of a characters physical fitness.  A character
with a high constitution will be resistant to injury and disease.  This ability
to resist injury is reflected in a character's hit points, the higher the Con, 
the higher the hit points.  The maximum constitution any character can achieve
is 25 points.

Cha - Charisma
Charisma is a character's natural ability to lead, reflection upon others, and
general persuasiveness are all measured in charisma.  A low charisma will limit
the amount of people who are willing to follow you, and will affect your inter-
actions with certain mobiles.  The maximum charisma any character can achieve is
25 points.

Lck - Luck
Luck represents your character's tendancy to succeed or prosper through chance or
good fortune.  As in life, it can be said that luck's influence on a character is
pervasive.  It can play a role in nearly every aspect to a small degree.  The
maximum luck any character can achieve is 25 points.

taught where an individual's pressure points are on an enemy.  Using this

The at command lets you perform an action in a room as if you were already
there.  The first argument is similar to the GOTO (q.v.) command, where you
give the name of a mob, player, or object, or a room number.  The second
argument is any command which you can perform.  Note this is very useful for
doing something in a room if you don't want to be seen there.  Use it with
care!  (Not all immortals can 'at' outside of their building zone!)

Examples:
    at 4503 red exit w -1   [Delete the west exit from room 4503 from
                             wherever you are]

An "evil" version of the Paladin, avengers are often set upon their 
path early on, by some traumatic experience in their past.  Seeking 
vengeance upon a single foe is often their formative experience, and 
then, achieving this, they boil over with hatred and strike out at others 
around them.  This class is inherently an evil one as their past and
actions dictate that they move toward vengenence, unlike their counterparts
the Paladin Class.

For those trained in the stealthy arts, a use of this skill attempts to place
your dagger or knife at precisely that spot in your opponents back where it will cause
the most damage.  This is a great way to start a fight while inflicting a 
surprise attack. Backstab will buff certain stats when used and will stack.

For those trained in stealth and such arts, this is an opening move. The use
of this skill places a "dot" on your victim, this causes a reduction in the
stopping power and silences the victim for a short duration. This is an excellent
way to start a fight while inflicting a surprise attack aswell as prventing an
enemy from casting upon you.

For those trained in the way of stealth and secrecy, this is an opening
attack that causes great damage to an opponent while putting a buff on you
simultaniously. This is a great way to start a fight and is a terrifying
surprise attack.

This is an attack that is to be used mid combat and is something that is only
trained in the arts of stealth and assassins. This causes a target to become
disoriented and dazes a target for a period of time, this causes the target
to disengage from combat for a period of time allowing for another opening
move or a stealthy escape.

Using your heroic ability, this will initiate a raged-strike at
your opponent, temporarily inflicting damage based on your killing
experience.

Cheapshot is used as an opening attack in fights. This attack is designed to
damage and stun an opponent, and is is mostly used in combination with other
openers or attacks.

Mute strike is an attack that will hit your opponent with a sound
suppressing effect, this attack is similar to strike with its
criticals. It also silences the opponent for a short duration, this
silence will last longer depending on how hard your mute strike lands.
This skill can be utilized during combat but has a cooldown to prevent
it from permanently silencing a foe.

Shadowform is an ability only taught to masters of the art of stealth and

Vanish is an ability learnt only by the higest masters of the art of stealth
and assasssination, this ability will disengage you from any combat and while

Barbarians hail mostly from the wastelands, any place which is

Brigands are bandits who have given up on working as mercenaries and instead 
make their living solely by wanton looting and pillaging. They conform to the

needs are taken care of.  Bandits and Brigands typically have up-to-date weaponry

Building an area is not a simple task, as you have many powerful yet
somewhat difficult tools at your disposal.  This list describes in brief
some of the more useful immortal commands available for builders.

    Building is not for everyone, we understand that.  If you find that
it's not all it's cut out to be for you, we'd appreciate if you were honest
and told us truthfully that you cannot handle the task and responsibility that
we demand from you.  To give you a better idea as to what is expected, these
help files, along with the Builder's Guide (see GUIDE_1, GUIDE_2, and GUIDE_3)
provide some examples and hints as to how you should go about creating an
area.

Redit  --  Your most useful tool, a "swiss army knife" type of utility.
           Reading the help on individual REDIT commands is a necessity

Rload  --  Loads your saved range (see RSAVE)

Rsave  --  Saves your assigned room range.  Do this often, please

Goto  --  Jump to a specific room number, mob, object, or player in the

Form  --  This will form a group of rooms en-masse.  Use this sparingly,

At  --  Perform a command AT a specific room, mob, object, or player in your

Mat  --  Perform an AT (q.v.) command at MANY rooms in your range

Rstat  --  Gives you statistics on a particular room

Offset  --  Sets your building offset

Clan Code Specifications V1.5

The purpose of the clan code is to provide code support for people joining clans. 
This support will allow clans some additional benefits such as clan-chat and will 
also recognise the role of clans within the social structure of the game. This is
 a first step in developing clans within the code structure of Perilous Realms and
 if successful future developments will follow.

An additional benefit of the clan code is that it is an upgrade of the exist 
choose protection against PKilling. The existing code is based on alignment and 
has given rise to many abuses. This also has the advantage of removing choose from 
alignment which has been causing problems for neutrals.
To explain the PK aspect of clans. All players are by default in the PROTECTED clan.
 This means that they have the same protection from PK as non-chosens currently do. 
They can't be attacked by another player. If you wish you may join the FREELANCE 
clan which makes you PK able. A protected player can join any clan. If they join a 
non-PK flagged clan, they retain their PK protection. If they leave that clan, 
they return to PROTECTED status. If they join a PK flagged clan then they become 
PK capable. If they leave that clan, they return to FREELANCE and may never join a 
non-PK clan. In this way you can choose between being PK and nonPK players but you 
can never change your mind once you've made the decision to become a PKer. For the 
same reason, a clan that is flagged nonPK cannot change to PK as it would set 
everyone in that clan to PK. If you wish to change your settings you'll need to set 
up a new clan and flag the new clan for PK and then your clanmembers can move over. 
Clan flags cannot be changed once a clan is active.

Clans will be defined in an offline text file which will use a form of tran to convert 
it to a game file. This means that changes in clan flags will be only possible by 
Assistant Imps and highers. In general, modifications to clan flags will NOT be permitted.

There will be three special pre-defined clans.

  newbie        - for those players under level 20
  protected     - for those players who do not wish to be
                  in a clan but wish to retain pk protection.
  freelance     - for those players who wish to be pk-capable
                  but who are not in clans.


When people reach level 20 they get automatically moved to the protected clan.

Clans will have attributes which will be defined by flags. These flags are as follows:

  PKA           - Allows members of this clan to PK all PK capable players.
  PKO           - Allows members of this clan to PK all PK capable players 
                  who are not clan members.
  PRIVATE       - on cwho (clan_who) you cannot see the clan allegiance.
                  Clan members can see their own clan members though.
  STEALTH       - as private, but not even clan members will be able to 
                  identify others of their own clan on clan_who.  

  - There are now 4 ranks of members: Members, Officers, Leader, Owner
  - There are no limits to the number of officers, leaders, or even owners, but use
    common sense.
  - An officer or higher can invite members to join at upto one rank lower
  - You can upgrade a players rank by inviting them again to the higher rank
  - An owner can invite a member as owner

Joining a Clan - CLANINVITE
To join a clan, a clan officer uses a command called CLANINVITE. 
Clan leaders and clan owners can issue CLANINVITE <name> <rank> to invite or promote 
a member to a higher rank 

The new member then needs to type CLANJOIN or CLANREJECT. You cannot be forced into a clan without 
your agreement. If the new member is a member of an existing clan, they cannot be 
entered into the new clan. In this case to join a new clan you need to leave your 
existing clan which you can do with CLANLEAVE.

Some clans are open enrollment. These do not require the permission of a clanmaster 
to join. To join these clans, the best example of which is FREELANCE, you type clanjoin 
freelance.
example:4 To go PK type CLANJOIN FREELANCE 0

You may not join a PK clan over level 300 if you are not already PK capable. This is 
to prevent people using their protected status to grow strong before risking PK as 
these people are known to abuse their strength to abuse weaker PK capable players.

Leaving a Clan - CLANLEAVE
To leave a clan, the member can type CLANLEAVE and the person will no longer be 
member of the clan. If the clanmaster types CLANLEAVE then the victim will be evicted
from their clan. When a clan member leaves a clan, the identifiers on the char-structure
indicated clan, clanmaster and the deputy need to be cleared. Maybe these should not be
left on the persons data structure but refered to the clan table as clanmasters may change
and this may cause issues with chars who have the other chars name still stored.

When leaving a PK clan, the player gets moved to the clan called FREELANCE. This is still
PK capable. If the person is in a non_pk clan then they moved to the protected clan.
This means that once you have joined a PK clan you can never obtain PK_protection again. 
This is the basic principle used to replace CHOOSE.

FORCED REMOVAL FROM A CLAN
A clanleader or the deputy can evict a member by using the command
4CLANEVICT <target>0.  This will remove the person from your 
clan.

CLAN CHANNEL (or CSAY)
Clan chat is a private global channel for clan members. Currently not implemented.

CLANWHO (or cwho)
This lets you see the clan allegiance of those players who are not set anonymous. 
Private members will also not be displayed unless you are of the same clan. 
Stealth members will never be displayed.

CLANLIST
This displays the clans in the game but does not display stealth clans. It should indicate
which clans are open-enrollment. 

MODE
You can identify which clan you are a member of by type MODES.

Please note if you are interested are interested in starting a clan, it is
certainly possible.  Please speak with an Implementor or and Assistant 
Implementor to find out the requirements and begin the process.

Clanlist lists all the existing clans, their names, whether
they are open access or whether they require an invitation
from the clan master.  They also provide information on the
PKilling status of the clan.

  -PK means they cannot PK
  +PK means they can.

The + means that that flag is set, a - sign means that it
is clear.

CLANWHO (command is cwho) allows you to see the clan membership
of people in the world.  Players who are set anonymous will have
their clan allegiance hidden.  Those who are in stealth and private
clans will also have their clan allegiances hidden.  However in 
private clans will see their own clan members, stealth clan members
will never have their allegiance shown, even to their own clan 
colleagues.

The class options within Perilous Realms are vast!  Each one of the
classes within the game have been designed and tuned to offer you the 
player a truely unique experience with each different class.  Sometimes
these differences are subtle will require you to pay special attention
to learn the neuances of that particular class.  Others in contrast can
be so different, you may find it a challenge to even begin to play it!

Again there are many different options on what you can choose to be; and
within the vast list of options there are classes that are dual or tri
style.  Meaning that a character can have certain characteristics of two
of three base style classes to create an even more powerful class!  These
dual and tri classes require more effort to level, so be warned there is
an investment of time and energy playing those types.  But they are alot
of fun, and are very powerful!  So whatever you choose, be aware that you
can always make another character to suite your playing style.  And above
all else, have fun!

The Cavalier class is the class of mounted warriors, knights who are a cut above the 
ordinary fighter both in combat ability and in social standing.  They generally have 
very high codes of honor, called Chivalry in the occident, Bushido for the oriental 
variant. Although cavaliers may use any weapons and armor, they have restrictions 
placed upon them in terms of their honor. As with weapons, the character's honor limits 
his armor choices.  Armor is more a badge of station than a means of protection.

Devoted to the service of their god, clerics are an integral part of 
society in Perilous Realms.  Though not the best fighters, their spells 
are sought out by all, and thier blessings can turn the tide of battle. 
A healer and a preist; working hard to bring honor and glory to their god
is what motivates the clerics of Perilous Realms to enter combat.  When
used in groups, they are renowned to extend the life expentance of their
comrads.

There are several things to remember in order to be successful in
combat.   The first is that you can attack a monster in five different
location: the feet, legs, arms, body and head.  Certain locations are
armoured differently, so those might be good places to strike.  Also,
hitting a limb does a bit less damage then hitting the head or body.
Plus, some armor absorbs physical damage...  Thus reducing the amount
of hitpoints both you and the mob will take.  Whenever you fight a monster
for the first time it would be wise to use the CONSIDER command first.
Doing so will immediately tell you if you should even attempt it.  With
the above in mind, here is an example:

Lashi considers killing a dragon.  He could attack in the body, head,
or a limb.  Lashi figures that the wings are fragile and are less
armoured than the body, thus he could hit the dragon more often there.
He also considers that a hit to the wing won't do as much damage as
a hit to the body.  Finally, he decides that, since the wing has less
stopping power, he could actually do more damage to the wing than
to the body.  

Following is a list of commands which let you inflict varying amounts of
pain on other creatures.  Some are more related to defensive tactics, but
all are somehow combat related:

Kill    --  Begin a hand-to-hand battle with one other creature (the hit
            command can be used in substitute for the kill command)

Kick    --  Aims a kick at your opponent

Bash    --  Attempt to knock your opponent sprawling on the ground.  You can
            hit him much harder when he's on the ground

Rescue  --  This command lets you jump in front of a fighting person and
            take their place in combat

Disarm  --  A successful disarm will knock the weapon out of an opponent's
            hands and send it flying across the room

Assist  --  Assisting a person will join into their fight against their
            opponent

Flee    --  When you are outmatched, it might be wise to beat a hasty retreat

Hitall  --  Initiates combat with all persons in the room.  Not a good command
            to typo in a crowded room

Backstab--  Usable only by those trained in the stealthy arts, this
            command will allow you to slip your dagger into someone's
            back.

Assa    --  This command is short for assassinate and is very simular to backstab.  
       The primary difference between the two commands is, backstab is meant
       to start a fight, while assassinate is an attempt to in one blow end
       the fight before it begins.

Aggr    --  This command will make you aggressive towards aggressive mobs.

Consider has been completely re-written to be more accurate.  It now
works by running a simulated combat between you and the monster and
seeing who will win...and by how much.  Thus, you could consider
a monster _during_ a fight and receive update information (you're
updated chance of victory).   Consider will also tell you the relative
height difference between you and the monster. (see HELP COMBAT)

Special Note:  Consider ONLY takes melee combat into account.   Things
like kick, bash, backstab, and spells are NOT considered.

Damroll is the representation of a ones ability to inflict damage on an opponent
with a normal attack.  Damroll in combination with strength and weapon dictates
the amount of total damage inflicted on each hit.  The higher the damroll, the better.

Death in the Perilous Realms mud is not as nasty of an experience as you 
might think.  We do suggest that you prevent it as much as possible but it 
happens to everyone, eventually.  

   System-wide there is a 4mortician0 available to help you regain your possessions
via your lost 4corpse0.  Should you die in a place that is systematically harder to 
get to or just plain impossible to find - the morticians in our world will help you out.

   It is also important to know that you can still retrieve your belongings within a 
time limit without loss of your equipment.  If you do not retreive your corpse
it will eventually fall apart and your objects and possessions will be exposed
to other players and worldly elements. 

   If you find yourself dead, you are exposed to a series of penalities that are
in place to help discourage you from dying.  The biggest penality is loss of
level.  The amont lost will vary, depending on age and size, and accumulated experience 
from your last level gain.  We are sorry if you think this is harsh but we feel overall 
it is a fair takeaway.  You may also lose Hitpoints, Mana, or other increases that are
 normally associated with levels.  

   If you are a choosen (player killer) and are killed, any other player killer can
take your belongings.

   The only other way a player may take the objects out of another player's corpse - is
by using the 4consent0 command.

This is used to calculate the damage in a lot of spells.  The spell 
defines an effective level, your current level less the level at 
which you learnt the spell plus one.  Thus when you learn a new spell,
you're at e-level 1 and it increases as you gain levels.  The e-level
maxes at 20.  The damage from spells using this formula is calculated
as the base damage (say 3d9) and multiplied by the e-level.  Thus as
you get more proficient, the strength of your spells increases.

riding as well as infantry fighting skills are those that can be counted

specifically trained strictly for mounted combat.  Due to a mixture of talents
and skillsets, the Dragoons developed a steathy means of calvary support while
bringing to the table mage type abilities.  Being warrior's at heart, when
dismounted a Dragoon is far deadlier in combat and most warriors.

The Druid is one with the natural lands - the forests, the mountains, the
lakes and seas, and all other places that form naturally in this realm.
The Druid is so in-tune with nature that they have the power to transform
themselves in beasts and mimic the awesome powers of such.  They have a 
small selection of spells from which to begin their adventuring career.

text:
Dwarves average four feet in height, with squat, broad bodies. Male dwarves 
grow thick facial hair. It is often a sign of extreme sadness and mourning 
for a dwarf to shave his beard. A majority of the dwavern race are spread out
throughout Perilous Realms, all in underground kingdoms or outposts.  While
located all over, the largest and most powerful nation is contained within
an underground city known as Fortrum. Most dwarf's will spend their life
in the underground working hard in mastering stone carving, metalworking or
some other labor intensive skill.  Due to this, they have a tremendous
constitution and are able to work for long days without rest.  Their single
minded nature though makes them less inclind to open ideas, and thus
affects their intelligence and charisma in a negative way.

carrying.  Realize some edibles are not healthy (i.e. poisoned) so it may
be a good idea to SIP or TASTE them at first to make sure it's ok to eat.

Slightly shorter than the average human, elves are also noticeably 
more slender and graceful which gives them a higher agility than most.  
All are handsome and beautiful averaging between four and a half to 
give and a half feet and weighing 95 to 135 pounds. Their slighter 
stature than some of the other races directly affect their durability 
or constitution.  Males are slightly more muscular on average, there is 
little difference in height between the sexes, and neither sex grows 
facial, nor body hair. Their features in general may be described as 
more angular and defined, including long, pointed ears and wide, 
almond-shaped eyes. Most elves have fair skin and dark hair, though this 
is no more true of all elves than it is of humans. It is openly known that 
althrough the elven race can be found all over Perilous Realms, but a major 
historical event encouraged them to as a race to take to the seas. Their 
kingdom and homeland is located somewhere within the great seas of 
Perilous Realms.

Life experience makes people unique, and your character is no exception.
Here is Perilous Realms, these life experiences are displayed in a simplified
mannor by means of levels.  Your character's skillset and its overall strength
power are directly linked to its current level.

You gain experience by: 

1. Killing an opponent
2. Inflicting damage upon an opponent 
3. Being part of a group that kills an opponent 
4. Succeeding while learning a skill or a spell through real world usage

Once you've gained sufficient experience you will know it!  Life Experience
combined with proper training will raise your level.  Each major city has within
its walls a guildmaster.  When you have reached the experience you need for the
next level, seek them out, they are always willing to help you progress a level.

When you reach a guildmaster you would use the GAIN command to increase your level.
If you so desire you may delay going to your guildmaster, and save up enough
experience points for up to three gains (or levels) at a time.  If you continue to
try to collect experience past this maxed cap of experience, it will not be applied
to your character.

Perilous Realms has a total of five hundred mortal levels.  After you have reached
level five hundred, you have the option to remortilize!

An expositor is a low ranking member of a religeous order.  Not a dedicated member
of the cloth like a cleric, an expositor is someone who is working to bring their
life in line with the standards set before them to join the order as a full member.
Expositor's come from all walks of life, but travel to and from cities all over the
Realms trying to convert those to worship their deity.  During their past course of
life they may have been bandits, warriors, or murders.  Hence when threatened they
do have significant proficiencies available to them for defense.  In addition in
their study and prayers, most deities bestow some minor abilities to help them show
potential converts the power of the gods.  With these abilities and backgrounds an
expositor may seem like a weaker class but can be a force to be reckoned with.

The forester usually held a position equal to a sheriff or local law enforcer. 
He is responsible for patrolling the woodlands on a lord or noble's property. 
His duties included negotiating deals for the sale of lumber and timber and 
stopping poachers from illegally hunting. Many times wanted criminals would 
hide in a forest. When this occurred it was the duty of the Forester to organize 
armed gangs to capture the criminal. Often foresters held titles of prominence 
in their local communities, and acted as barristers and arbitrators.  A forester
has also been know to study some minor arcane arts to help him in his duties.
Failing to protect the land he has been assigned over could result in being
him removed or worse executed if the landowner was powerful enough.

Standing ten to twelve feet tall, a single giant weighs approximately 
sixteen hundred pounds. It is an immensely powerful creature nearly as 
agile as its human forebears. Its facial features are human, but locked 
into a naturally dour, even menacing expression. Like many of the 
uncivilized races, giants are generally raised within a tribal community.
Giants being so physically massive, have historically relied on their 
strength and ability to absorb damge instead of using tact in altercations.  
As such, giants have a strength and constitution that are second to none 
amongst the mortal races of Perilous  Realms. Because of relying for 
centuries on their brawn and not their brains, giants tend to be deficient 
with their intelligence, and wisdom.  With their massive size, it also 
causes them to be slightly slower than most humans and their dexterity 
suffers.  But to survive so long as a race, only using their brawn there

    go n                    ; move north once
    go gates                ; enters the gates

You can repeat a move by tying a number in front of it:

    go 3se                  ; move southeast 3 times

Gold coins are used to buy things you want or need in the realms. They can
normally be found on monsters or people who would normally carry money. Don't
expect to many dogs or cats to be running around with a big stash of money.
You might occasionally spot a few coins in a birds nest though.. Money is a 
hard thing to come by and will normally be found in larger quantities on the
tougher monsters or people of high stature (or if you are real daring maybe
a dragon will loan you a few gold..). Just because one monster does not have

Gnomes stand three to three and a half feet tall and weigh forty to forty 
five pounds. Their skin color ranges from dark tan to woody brown, their 
hair is fair, and their eyes can be any shade of blue. Gnomes are naturally 
friendly, highly social and fun loving people. They are respected by Elves 
for their communion with nature and knowledge of arcane magic, admired by 
Hobbits for their humor, and sought out by Dwarves for their gemcutting 
skills.  Gnomes being highly social and skilled in tinkering tend to be 
very intelligent.  At times their inability to fully apply that intelligence 
leads some gnomes to be less wise than other races.  In addition, some

and as such their charisma can suffer.

This document is not intended as a guide to the mechanics of building;
that can be found in the documentation for the mud/commands. Instead,
this document is a generic guide to writing good descriptions.
Note that throughout this document the word object has been used to
denote any distinct thing in the database, whether that be a room,
exit/action, object, player, or whatever.

1. A Guide to Good Building
Good building encompasses more than just writing a description for
every object that is created; it involves careful consideration of
what the object is, how it fits in with every other object, and...

2. Coherence and Theme
No database object exists in vacuum, and it is necessary to keep this
in mind whenever creating a new object. Everything created must fit
within the framework established by the other objects in the database
- not only the individual objects themselves, but also the atmosphere
and world milieu.

3. The Nature of Descriptions
Descriptions are the means by which the players sense their
surroundings, and as such are very important. Descriptions serve two
main functions: to inform the player of what they sense, and to
express the theme. Both of these aspects will be discussed below.

4. Sensing the World
Since a character receives input about the world in the most part from
descriptions, it is vital that these descriptions follow certain
guidelines, in order that journeying through the world is as rich and
full an experience as possible.

5. Making it Coherent and Real
A description, as well as giving the players solid information, such
as what an object looks like, should also convince the player that the
object is real. The first thing that needs to be done is to make
objects mentioned in a description, particularly a room description,
actual objects. This allows the player to at least attempt
manipulating them, and ensures that a player will never receive that
most irritating of messages "you see no <object> here." when in the
description of the room clearly states that that object is present.
At least include an extra description for all objects listed if not
the actual object.

On a wider level, an object should fit in with the other objects in
the vicinity. That is, create a reality out of the combined effect of
many objects seen at once. For while each individual object may be a
beautifully described creation, together they might create a confusing
and conflicting image, rather than a coherent one. Care must therefore
be taken that the overall effect suits what is wanted, in addition to
each distinct object following the other guidelines set out in this
document.

There are a couple of aspects to creating this coherence. One is the
writing style. It is important to be consistent in the treatment of
all the objects in an area, unless one or two are deliberately made to
stand out - although the individual descriptions will not be the same,
if they are approached with the same style, they will be lent a degree
of coherence.

The second aspect is the use of detail to build up a coherent picture
- that is, to include objects which fit in with the area as a whole.
For example, a bedroom would clearly require a bed, and could
reasonably be expected to contain a container of some sort for
personal items, a wardrobe, and such like things. By presenting
sufficient detail, not just in the descriptions but also in the actual
objects included, a coherent and real picture can be created more
easily in the minds of the players.

6. too much detail vs not enough
When writing descriptions, it is essential that enough information is
presented so that the player can get a good idea of the main features
of the object, while at the same time not inundating him/her with useless
detail.

Try to think of what you would take note of if you saw the object, and
what words you would use to describe it to someone who wasn't able to
sense it. It might well be useful to actually do the latter for real,
to get an idea of what is distinctive about the object. As a general
guide, for actual objects, mention size, colour and shape to begin
with, since these are usually basic to every object and a person's
perception of them.

Beware of simply using an established, abstract noun to describe
something - for example, "church". This is both far too bland, in that
it does not give an accurate picture of the building, and yet also
provokes a large number of (possibly) unwanted connotations from the
mind of the player. Although this might help to make the scene more
vivid for the reader, it is encouraging the player to see the world
entirely from his/her own perspective, with little actual input from the
description. It is better instead to use more and specific words to
build up a picture which carries its own connotations, giving a solid
framework which the players can adorn with their own imaginations.
However, descriptions should not overwhelm players through their size,
nor indeed through an abundance of detail. It is vital that they have
enough undefined or "grey" areas that the imaginations of the players
can use to customise the description so that it becomes meaningful to
them.

7. Using levels of scale
One good way of presenting lots of interesting details, without having
them all overwhelm the player when she looks at the object, is to use
multiple levels of scale. That is, using nested "levels" of detail
which expand upon a certain part of the description given in the
"level" above; in effect each level is accompanied by a reduction in
scale.

For example, a statue may be described as consisting of a plinth and a
main piece of sculpture. The character may then look at the plinth,
and see a description of it, perhaps saying that there is some
engraving on it, some text and a frieze. The character may then
examine the frieze and the text in more detail, or decide to look at
the main piece of sculpture, which might in turn lead to other levels
of detail.

Using this technique, lots of information can be presented, without
being obtrusive; any level of detail can be achieved. It needs to be
said, however, that this method can be frustrating for the reader; if
a number of options are presented in each level of description, and
this is done for multiple levels, then the reader might end up
spending large amounts of time simply rereading descriptions in order
to remember which options she has not explored. The larger the "tree"
of descriptions, the more of a problem this becomes.

At the opposite extreme, there is little point in presenting a level
of detail which opens out onto only one lower level of detail; the two
should be amalgamated, in order to keep the "tree" trim, and to save
frustration for the players.

8. using all the senses
There is a tendency when writing descriptions to present exclusively
visual data, remembering the other senses only when the object is in
some way "special". It is also common for some objects to be given
much greater attention than others. Not only is this unrealistic, but
it also leads to the attitude among players that these objects are
important, while those which aren't given such treatment are not
important. Thus the author is imposing his/her own idea of what is
important on the players, rather than letting them decide for
themselves. This is to be avoided.

All descriptions should be well balanced, with each sense catered for
(if information is appropriate - if information for a certain sense is
not expected (for example, the smell of metal) then this should be
omitted). Admittedly many inanimate objects have little or no smell
that humans can detect, and do not of themselves make noise; however,
where this is a part of the object, they should be included. Also,
every object has a texture, and many will taste of something, even
though it may be hard to define just what. (obviously most of this
wont exist for the room object)

9. Problem of Omnisciency
Never include anything in a description which draws on data other than
that which can be gained via the senses of the players. Indeed, try to
present only information that is minimally interpreted, or which most
if not all characters can reasonably be assumed to interpret in the
same way. By interpretation I mean the process whereby a person
senses, say, writing, rather than unrelated blobs of black. This must
be done, of course; however, it should be done to as minimal extent as
possible, while still maintaining easy comprehensibility among the
vast majority of players.

The intent of this approach is to force the player to be aware of his/her
surroundings, and to ensure that the player does not gain information
without expending some thought to do so. If it is possible to write a
description from which information can be inferred, (either with or
without additional character knowledge) then it should be written in
this way, rather than presenting that information outright.

Not only is what is said in a description important, but also the way
in which it is said. By presenting information in the way in which a
resident of the world would have seen or described it, the players
will be forced to adopt some of same paradigms of thought as those in
the world have.

10. ** Never Assume **
Don't assume anything about the direction from which a player enters
the room.  That is, don't write descriptions that look like this:
"The hallway stretches out before you to the north.  You aren't sure
whether you should go that way or not."

This description only makes sense if the player is coming from some
direction other than north.

Perilous Realms makes a clear distinction between in character and out of
character concepts.  From the moment you connect to the mud and enter the game,
to the time you leave, you should remain "in character" or IC, except for
special circumstances.  (Believe it or not, there are times when you have to
express something in OOC terms, like getting up to go to the bathroom, or 
getting a drink, or your dog is on fire.)

Staying in character is more than just using obscure terms to refer to the
game around you.  When you are in character, you should try to think and 
act as your character, not as yourself.  You may be a short, pimply teenager
with glasses, but to everyone else, you should try to portray yourself as 
your character, be it a cruel warrior, a benevolent priest, or an evil 
mage.  Following the guidelines set to define the IC/OOC distinction (see 
help GUIDELINES) may be difficult at first, but accomplishing your goals 
by staying in character can be immensely more rewarding than mindless 
hack and slash.  In fact, playing in the Perilous Realms world as if it 
were a hack and slash genre will probably result in less success than if 
you play within the system.

    We here at Perilous Realms have a complex world for you to adventure in
as your character.  Try to see the world as your character would, 
including the fact that you must take into consideration that YOU the 
player knows more than your character.  For example, a young, naive  
dwarf, coming from a society and a culture where magic is rare and 
feared, upon seeing a very powerful magic item, would not immediately 
know it's value, use, or properties, and would most likely either ignore 
it, or should he know of it's attributes, may even try to destroy it.  
(Note: this is just an EXAMPLE, you are expected to handle each situation 
you face with a modicum of originality and cleverness.)  You are expected to
keep OOC knowledge (such as "spells" and "characters") just there, OUT
of character, and OUT of the game.  There will be no sharing of OOC 
information within the game, whether communicated in an IC manner, or an 
OOC manner.
    Another aspect of remaining in character is that YOU the player and your
character may have different senses of value, customs, and beliefs.  You 
may see that sword lying by the roadside as a piece of junk, but your 
character may pick it up to examine it, admire its worksmanship, perhaps 
wonder where it came from or who lost it there.  Perhaps your
character has an aversion to blood, and at the first sight of it lapses 
into a swoon.  Not all characters will be without flaws, just like in 
real life we are not all perfect.  Don't try to play your character as 
the "perfect warrior" or the "most powerful mage."  While something like 
that may become one of your goals as a character, you won't get there without
years (game time years) of in character work and effort.
    Above all, remember that your main goal should not be to get "the 
best equipment" or to get "the highest level," but to play out your 
character successfully.  Getting the best equipment and becoming a 
highly-respected character are certainly OOC goals to work towards, but 
concentrating on staying IC as best as you can will most likely result in 
your OOC goals of power coming true anyway.

Immortals are the administrative aspect of the game.  While is it
certainly possible to create a game that is 100% automated, Perilous
Realms has an administrative staff that works to constantly improve
your (the player's) experience.  Weither its creating unique quests,
creating new areas for you to explore, or adding code to increase
the versitility of the game, the Immortals are working for you.

With that being said, in general, immortal's are busy people and
may be unavailable.  However if you do end up seeing one that is
visible, and have established contact, please keep in mind some
important things that they will NOT help you with.

Immortals will not help you:

Get Equipment
Kill Mobs
Restore your Character on Request
Anything in General that would give you an unfair advantage.

Immortals will help you:

If you find a bug (even if they can't fix it themselves or
reimburse you themselves).
If you have a question that is not listed in the helpfiles.
Need clarification of a law.

                        |  LAWS OF PERILOUS REALMS  |
                        []-------------------------[]  


Respect is the number one law of Perilous Realms.  The principle of showing
respect to your fellow players, and the immortal staff is the basis of these
laws.  Obviously it isn't possible, nor practical to write down hundreds of
things you can and can not do.  However we do have some guidelines that help
define what should be viewed as legal and what should be viewed as illegal.
Please keep these very important points in mind while you are connected to
Perilous Realms.  Again just because it isn't written here, it doesn't mean 
its legal or illegal.  If an immortal asks you to desist something, please
do so immediately.

Respect:          
                1. Never use foul language toward a fellow mortal or immortal.
                2. Do not steal another player's kills, you are on your honor
                   to refrain from doing this. (Ie. Don't walk into a room
         and begin attacking a monster they are fighting, unless you're
         grouped)
                3. Do not summon aggressive mobs to Midgard. (You must be at
                   least a dozen rooms outside Midgard to do this)
                4. Do not harass or annoy another player intentionally.

MultiPlaying:
                Read "help multiplaying" for detailed information. One account
                per person.

Immortals:
                1. If you find yourself unsure about something it is always   
                   all right to ask an immortal, they will be more than happy
                   to answer your questions.
                2. Do not ask an immortal to reimburse you for eq/gold/levels
                   lost unless it is a game error.
      3. See "help immortal" for more information

Charmed Mobs:
                1. Do not attack another player's charmed mobs.
                2. Do not order your pet to attack another player.
                3. Do not give any eq or weapons to a mob unless they are
                   currently charmed by you.
      4. Do not used your charmed mobs to spam over characters.

General Advice:
                1. Check the mortal/immortal boards frequently to keep up
                   with coding changes and what is going on in the game.
                2. Don't portal to areas that are off limits due to your 
                   level.
                3. Don't exploit any bug in the game.  Doing so will result
                   in deletion and site banning. However, reporting bugs
                   result in very nice compensation.

Universal Channels-
        Gossip:
                1. Do not gossip anything game-related (i.e. where is Puff?)
                2. You may talk about almost anything not game-related.
                   (movies, books, TV shows, etc)
                3. Do not tell your personal statistics on gossip. (hp's, etc)
                4. Do not use gossip for auctions, and vise versa. 
                5. Do not gossip something more than once. (Help Spam)
                6. Do not gossip anything about how bad your lag is, or 
                   anything closely related.
                7. Do not swear, or use language which would offend anyone
                   over gossip. (Jesus Christ, and basically all swear words)
                8. Do not gossip anything that is not in English (Spanish,
                   French, German, etc)

       Auction:
                1. Do not say something that would be considered a gossip on 
                   auction (as stated above).
                2. When auctioning something state the name and minimum bid
                   of the item, nothing more. (Humming Gauntlets 50k min)
                3. Do not give out ANY statistics on the item over auction, if
                   you so desire to over tells it is allowed.
                4. Do not ask for equipment over auction.  Shouting is allowed
                   for this.
                5. Do not spam auction, as well as gossip.
                6. Five minutes is the maximum for one item to be auctioned.
                7. Only one item is to be auctioned at a time.
                8. Three minutes without a bid is the minimum time before you
                   may withdraw an item from auction.
                9. If a bid is made that matches your minimum you must sell.
               10. If your bid is the final bid you must pay for the item unless
                   the seller agrees otherwise.
               11. NO FAKE BIDS!
               12. No bidding for other pc's
         
Semi-Global Channel(s)-
         Shout:
                1. You may shout for asking for spells, asking for equipment, 
                   offering trades, etc.
                2. Do not shout anything profane.

The Game (Killing, Pkilling, Arenas, etc)-
        Arenas:
                1. Do not steal from people in an arena.
                2. Do not use charmed mobs in an arena.
                3. Do not teleport opponents out of the arena.
                4. Do not summon others who are in an arena, whether you are
                   in it or not.
                5. Do not group with anyone in the arena.  Ganging up on
                   somebody is one thing, but you may have nasty spells cast
                   on you if you actually group with someone.
      Pkilling:
                1. Do not attack or harrass a newbie, under level 20, at any cost, 
                   this is strictly enforced.
                
 A Final Note-
        Rules are subject to change at any time, we will make every effort
        to keep the helpfiles up to date.  You can find information on any
        changes in the helpfiles, the message of the day (MOTD), and the
        immortal board in the underground.

*       And the most important rule of all: Have alot of fun, that is what 
        it's all about.

Lizardfolk are primitive reptilian humanoids typically standing from six to 
seven feet tall. Their scales are normally dull, earthy colors such as green, 
brown, or gray. They have a tail for balance, which measures three to four 
feet long. Typical weight is between 200 and 300 pounds. Lizardfolk are omnivores, 
though they have a preference for meat.  Lizardfolk are normally found in temperate 
marshes and swamps.  The lizardfolk with their unusual body proportions are able
throw their bodies around with great agility.  Their nature of spending a good
portion of their life in a marsh swimming, makes then a little less hardier than
most races raised on land.  Their foul smell and primitive almost barbaric culture
makes many people look down upon them.

The five primary hit locations are: feet, legs, body, arms, head.
For monsters whose anatomy doesn't quite match up to a humanoid's,
the locations are substituted with more realistic ones.  For
example, a dragon might have locations claws, legs, body, wings, head
or a spider might have feet, legs, body, legs, head.

When you attack a certain location, whether or not you hit depends
on the relative height differences and how well the location is
armored.  A giant would have an easy time hitting a gnome's head,
but the gnome would have a bit of difficulty hitting the giant's!

Hitting a certain location also has the potention of doing more
or less damage.  For example, hit a hit to the arm scores only
80% of the damage a hit to the body would.

Consider all of this when initiating combat.

Mages are very weak fighters when it comes to hand to hand battle, 
but upon the aquiring of a spell repitoire can become quite powerful.

Character's that are of the Cleric type or variety utilize mana to cast their
spells.  Mana is a force that is bestowed onto the character through their
deity.  Because this mana is a blessing bestowed onto characters, it is 
something set aside for a dedicated purpose.  Thus when casting spells with
a cleric type, spells will not be warped by the presence of iron as some mages
would, it is used to bring honor and glory to the caster's deity.  Being that

A mercenary, also known as, Professional Soldier, Soldier of Fortune, Swashbuckler, 
or Profitmaker, is a person who takes part in an armed conflict who is not a national 
or a party to the conflict and is "motivated to take part in the hostilities essentially 
by the desire for private gain and, in fact, is promised, by or on behalf of a party 
to the conflict, material compensation substantially in excess of that promised or paid 
to combatants of similar ranks and functions in the armed forces of that Party".  Because
of the broad nature required to servive the profession of being a mercenary, they are 
trained to be soldiers first, stealthy agents second, and when all else fails, unleash 
the arcane arts on their foes.

The name of the town of Midgard is defined by scholars as the "middle enclosure".
As such it is a fitting description for the largest town in the world of Perilous
Realms.  Midgard is the center of bustling activity within the realm.  Races from
all over can be found there, looking for military training, merchant opportunities, or
arcane research.  In fact midgard is so well established there are only a few things
that an adventurer couldn't find there.  The history of the city is surrounded by
strife, civil war, invading armies, and other cataclismic events.  As such the
evidence of such conflicts can be seen all over the city, and serve as a reminder
to the lessons learned from the past.  Much effort has been put into making sure
the history of the past isn't repeated, as such the library within Midgard has many
books and scrolls concerning the history of Perilous Realms.  Maps are posted all 
over the city in order to keep visitors from getting lost within its vastness.  By 
typing Map while in the city you are able to briefly look at the closet map.

Midgard is also the in the racial capitol for the human race.

Miller Falls was known as the only trading port connected to the ancient continent.
A city that used it wealth to enrich itself with glorious splender and only the
finest amenities.  Several years ago during a peroid of unsually heavy storms, the
seawalls protecting the harbor began to fail.  And the river near the city began to
swell.  The citizens in a panic began taking down their fortified walls, and throwing
the debris onto the seawall to keep it intact.  Unknowingly though, they opened a
means for the swollen river to enter the great city.  Once the flooding river entered
the city, it all was underwater.  Months later, when the water receeded, it was
noticed that many didn't make it out in time and still over a third of Miller Falls 
was underwater.  Thus the city as a whole was abandoned, but a few brave souls still 
work the habor and piers, fishing and providing ferry services.

"Message Of The Day" - MOTD

This command lists important system announcements.  It would be wise to check
it often, as you ARE responsible for knowing its content.  Ignorance of the law 
is no excuse for breaking it, as whenever the motd is changes you must select it
before you are allowed to enter the game.

If your new to mudding, or someone just invited you to look into Perilous 
Realms, the following descriptions of what we are may be helpful.

A MUD, is a multiplayer real-time virtual world, with the term usually 
referring to text-based instances of these. Perilous Realms combines elements 
of role-playing, hack and slash, player versus player, interactive fiction, 
and online chat. (NOTE:  Role-playing is NOT a requirement, it can add depth
to your experience here, but certainly is not a manditory requirement.)

Players can read or view descriptions of rooms, objects, other players, 
non-player characters, and actions performed in the virtual world. Players 
typically interact with each other and the world by typing commands that 
resemble a natural language.

Perilous Realms set in a fantasy world populated by fictional races and monsters, 
with players choosing classes in order to gain specific skills or powers. The 
objectives of Perilous Realms are to slay monsters, explore a fantasy world, complete 
quests, go on adventures, create a story by roleplaying, and advance the created 
character. Due to the very nature of the game, there is no way to "win", but
rather it provides an environment that you can create your own destiny.  You are
able to experience classes, clans, monsters, and story lines from multiple angles
and literally provide endless hours of entertainment.  It is not unusual to
run into someone who has been playing here for over ten plus years.

This is very important information. Read it understand it and follow it.
This may seem to be "harsh" but we want a good and fair environment.  Other
games may permit this provision, however in Perilous Realms we have a
special account system that deals with multiple characters at once.
Because of this, all characters are linked to one account.  One account
per player, any additional accounts constitutes multiplaying.

There is NO multiple playing allowed. An example of multiplaying would be
logging in a high level character to almost kill a mobile, then logging
off said character to kill with a lower level character to reap the benefits.

STORAGE characters are NOT allowed. A storage character would be a
character that holds items or equipment that you don't want on your person
at a given time.  If you want storage, we offer the option of housing in
which storage lockers can be purchased and used for storage.

PUNISHMENT for multiplaying:

First offense: Banshment to hell for 2 days of both players.
Seconf offense: Banishment for 2 weeks.
Third offense: Deletion of both players.

This is NOT negotible and WILL be carried out.  The rules are here to keep
the game fair, please follow them.

This is a list of basic commands you will use to move yourself around
the game world.  Also included is a list of commands to change your position.
Whether you are sitting, standing, or otherwise resting affects how quickly
you recover from both physical and mental exhaustion.

North, East, West, South, NE, NW, SE, SW, Up, Down  
       --  The basic directions, as well as UP and DOWN will move you
           in that direction.  Pretty self explanatory.  Note that if
           you are falling DOWN, you may not be able to stop yourself

Go     --  Allows you to move quickly around the world by entering a
           list of directions and/or exits.  (See GO for details)
           For example, from Bounce: 'go 2u 5w 10s shop' will take you to
           the Magic Shop.

Enter  --  Allows you to enter a specifically denoted exit in the room

Leave  --  Similar to ENTER, but works only if you are inside

Stand  --  If you are reclining (see REST) or sitting (see SIT) this will
           stand you upright on your own two feet (or more, if you have them)

Sit    --  This command places you in a sitting position

Rest   --  This command will sprawl you out on the floor (or ground) in a
           rather leisurely position until you STAND or SIT up. When resting 
      you regenerate hit points, moves, power, and mana.


Sleep  --  When you get tired, you can sleep for a while.  Note that when
           you are asleep the only recognized command is WAKE, and you are
           in a rather vulnerable position.  When sleeping you regenerate
      hit points, moves, power, and mana.

Wake   --  If you are asleep, this command will wake you up and place you
           in a sitting position.

Follow --  If you don't know the way, you can tag along behind someone with
           this command.  Also is a requirment to be in a group.

Hide   **  Only those specially trained in the stealthy arts can perform
           this task.  If successful, you duck behind the nearest object and
           try to not be seen

Sneak  **  Only those specially trained in the stealthy arts can perform
           this task.  If successful, you can progress unnoticed past people
           and enter and leave the room quietly
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
For additional help on any of these topics, see their respective help pages.

We are honored that you've taken the time to join us, hopefully your experience here 
will be enjoyable. Most (not all) are generally very helpful and willing to spend some
time showing you the ropes and answering any questions you may have.

Use these help files to get acquainted with our world:

This is a long list of commands you can use to manipulate objects
in the game.  Also listed here are eating commands, door manipulation, and
banking commands.

Get, Take  --  Will cause you to get an object from various places

Hold, Grab  --  Will take a firm hold on an object in your off-hand

Drop  --  Drops a particular item on the ground

Examine  --  Take a good hard look at an object.  If you are knowledgeable
             in certain skills, you may get more information about the
             object than one who does not

Use  --  This allows you to use a wand or staff.  You must be holding it for
         this command to work

Junk  --  Causes you to break an object beyond repair.  Be sure you really
          mean it!

Wear  --  Wear a particular object on a particular body part

Wield  --  Ready a weapon for combat in your strong hand, or both if it's
           really big

Remove  --  Negates a WEAR, WIELD, HOLD, or GRAB command and places the
            object in your INVENTORY.  You will drop it if you are already
            burdened down

Inventory  --  Lists everything you are carrying

Equipment  --  Lists everything you are wearing

Give  --  Give something you are holding to another person

Quaff  --  Drink a potion that you are holding

Recite  --  This command allows you to read off a magic scroll, invoking its
            power to do something useful (or harmful, sometimes)

Lock  --  If you have the right key, this locks a door, chest, gate, etc...

Unlock  --  Opposite of LOCK, also requires you have the key

Open  --  Opens an UNLOCKed door, chest, gate, etc...

Close  --  Closes an OPEN door, chest, gate, etc...  Beware that some of
           these will lock automatically

Pick  **  Usable only by those trained in the arts of pilfering, this command
          if successful will allow the trained burgular to skillfully unlock
          a locked object

Eat, Drink  --  When you get hungry or thirsty, these commands will allow
                you to satisfy your hunger or thirst, provided that you have
                something to consume

Sip, Taste  --  These are "reduced" versions of the above, useful to "test"
                food or drink to see if it is perhaps poisoned.  Consuming
                less of the offensive material will lessen the effect

Fill  --  This command will let you fill one drink container from another

Pour  --  This command will ungraciously dump the contents of your drink
          container onto the ground

Slice  --  If you have the stomach for it, you can barbarically slice up
           a dead body and use it for food

Deposit  --  If you're at a bank, you can deposit money or items (for a fee)
             and keep them safe

Withdraw  --  If you're at a bank, this command lets you take out money or
              items which you deposited

Balance  --  Shows you how much money you have in the bank
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
For additional help on any of these topics, see their respective help pages.

Power is the numerical value of how much mental energy a mage type has.  Mage

desired affect (casting a spell in this case).  Because of this channeling,

in which their energy is displaced or channeled elsewhere.  There are places
within Perilous Realms that offer true mental solace, and will provide a mage
type much faster power regeneration.

Usage: Kills

The kills command is used in two ways, first and most importantly it gives you a
detailed list of the last twenty mobs (or monsters) that you've killed.  This
list is important, because it helps you keep track of how many times you have
killed each type of monster.  The more times you manage to slay each creature,
the more it becomes second nature and part of habbit.  As such after you've killed
a particular type of monster a large amount of times, you will notice that your
experience gained from said monster isn't as large as it once was.

Fighting in groups is a great way to avoid the habbitual slaying of monsters, as
when you work in the chaos of a number of people in combat its never the same ole
thing.  Because of this, mobs that you kill while in a group are not added to your
kills list.

Secondly, using the kills command while in the Underground Tavern within Midgard will
have you look at the posted list of the most accomplished adventurers in Perilous
Realms.

If you ever find yourself needing to clear your kills list to help you continue
leveling, there are options available.  A death within the realms gives you a clean
slate in this regard, and there are also rumors of alchemists that can brew potions
that will give you a new outlook on combat, these potions will clear you kill list...

Perilous Realms supports a flexible prompt system.. You can configure the prompt
however you like best.

We now can also support COLOR and multi line prompts and if you support true
vt100 you can have nonscrolling prompts along with whatever else you can dream
up.  SEE PROMPT CODES for a listing of some of the escape codes you can use.

Syntax:
    prompt list
    prompt 'format'
    prompt number

The first form displays a list of pre-made prompts that you may find somewhat
useful, or you may wish to make your own, as described below.

With prompt 'format', format is as follows:

Characters in the format string not following a % sign are echoed back
out in your prompt.  The % is the prefix character for certain types of
substitutions.  Here is a sample prompt command line:

        prompt 'H:%h M:%m V:%v> '

Your prompt would then look like:
H:104 M:100 V:140>

Which mean you currently have 104 hp, 100 mana, and 140 movement points.

Here is a complete list of the % commands.  Case is IMPORTANT.
%h - Current hit points
%H - Maximum hit points
%m - Current mana
%M - Maximum mana
%p - Current power
%P - Maximum power
%v - Current Movement
%V - Maximum Movement
%E - Current energy (only for Th/As classes)
%R - Current rage (only for Wa/Bb classes)
%u - other group members colored by condition and underlined if being attacked
%U - other group members and %hp, name colored by condition and underlined if being attacked
%o - Opponent condition
%O - Name of opponent colored by condition
%i - If you are invisible will display I for invis, otherwise, blank
%l - Percent of maximum hp of leader
%L - Name of leader
%x - Current experience points
%X - Experience needed for level (negative if you can advance)
%g - How much gold you have
%G - How much gold you have in the bank
%c - Current amount of combo points applied (only for some melee classes)
%C - Maximum combo points appliable (only for some melee classes)
%% - translated to just a % sign


Immortal Only
%r - Current room number
%I - Invis level
%F - Flags currently set (stealth, away, nohassle)
%S - Name of person you are currently snoping

There are also a few \ escape sequences (More in HELP CODES):
\e - escape for making nifty prompts with color etc
\n - newline
\r - carriage return
\\ - echo a single \

Example prompts (using escape codes, this is not necessary it just makes them
look alot neater):

prompt '\e[47;31mH:%h\e[32m M:%m\e[34m V:%v\e[30m>\e[0m '   (H M V  in color)
prompt '\e[40;31mH:%h\e[32m M:%m\e[34m V:%v\e[37m>\e[0m '   (reverse of above)
prompt '\e[1mH:%h>\e[0m '      (hp in intense white)
prompt '\e[47;30mH:%h>\e[0m '   (hp on a reverse video background)
usage:
prompt          or
prompt list     or
prompt <# from list>    or
prompt <string>

This command deletes an extra field from the room record.  The keyword list
must exactly match the keyword list of the extra you wish to delete.  So

Input a description for the room you are in (or AT (q.v.))  Descriptions
should be fairly complete and accurate, but excluding any "transient"
features such as people or removable objects.  "Static" features such as
chairs, tables, and rocks should also have an EXTRA (q.v.) description
attached to them.  If description_text is omitted, you will be prompted
for a multi-line description.  There should be no reason unless you are
doing special rooms, that you have a one-line description.

Note: if you have certain things in a room you want people to be able to
use (such as a hole in the wall) you can create a notake object with a
hidden flag (lets say its a hole) and it will not show as "a hole is here"
but they will be able to do things with it such as get things out of it
(assuming you made it a container).

Examples:

    red desc This is a boring room.

The first form sets door flags on each side of the exit, while the second
sets it on only one side (the current side.)  Dir is the direction (or number)
of the exit you wish to modify, and flags is a list of one or more dflags
listed below.

Examples:
    red dflag 10 door locked    [Exit #10 is a locked door]
    red dflag ne autoclose      [The ne exit closes automatically]

Dflags:
door - You need this if you want players to be able to OPEN and CLOSE (q.q.v.)
       the door.  Closed doors do not show up in EXITS (q.v.)
closed - The "initial" state of the door will be closed.  In other words, when
         the game loads (reboot, crash, etc.) the door will be closed.  You
         want this on a door which you want to be hard to get through, if it's
         not there players can walk through it when they get there.
locked - Same as 'closed' dflag, but the door will also be locked on "initial"
         reloads.  Door must be 'closed' to also be 'locked' initially.
secret - A 'secret' door will not be seen unless it's specifically looked for,
         or if the player has a sense of where secret things are (i.e. thieving
         types, and such.)
pickproof - If flagged with this, a door cannot be PICKed (q.v.) by thieves.
            Use this where applicable, a farmers hut for example would most
            likely be easy prey for a thief's pick, whereas the gate to the
            emperor's mansion would DEFINITELY be pickproof (and most likely
            not 'knockable' as well -- see below.)
knockable - If so flagged, the door can be the target of magic designed to
            open locked doors.  This is counter-intuitive to other flags, as
            this flag when present ALLOWS the action, rather than prevents it.
hidden - When flagged 'hidden' a door cannot be seen by anyone.  There should
         be sufficient clues in the description or extras as to the presence
         of the door (or exit.)
message - A 'message' flag on the door lets a message be displayed when a
          player walks through the exit.  The messages are in the form of
          extras (_ex## -- where ## is the numeric exit from RSTAT (q.v.))
autoclose - If a door is flagged 'autoclose' it will slam shut behind the
            player when he walks through it.  Anyone following him in a group
            will also pass through before the door shuts.
autolock - When combined with 'autoclose' also locks the door after it shuts
           behind the player(s).
Same as red_dflags except its for one way doors. See red_dflags for full info.

This command turns an already-existing exit into a door.  The direction
can be an actual direction, or a numerical exit number.  The key can be
either an object number which will unlock the door, or -1 for no key.
If a list of keywords (e.g. 'oak door') is specified, it must be in single
quotes (').  Door flags can be one or more of the following self-explanatory
codes: door hidden locked closed lockable pickproof knockable autolock
       autoclose secret message

It would be wise if you want your door to BE a door, you give it at least
the 'door' flag.  Also, provide keywords so the door can actually be referred
to by name.

Examples:
    red door n 123 'oak door' locked closed
        [makes a door in the north wall that is closed and locked]
        [...object #123 will unlock the door]
    red odoor w -1 'gate' closed
        [makes a one way door to the west, with keyword gate]
usage:
redit door <direction> <key> [keyword list] [flags]
redit odoor <direction> <key> [keyword list] [flags]

text: Same as red_door except its for one way doors. See red_door for full info.

This will describe the exit in the direction specified.  Players may then
LOOK (q.v.) at the exit and get something more descriptive than "You see
nothing special..."  If you do not enter a description, you will be
prompted for one (same format as red_desc and red_extra (q.q.v))

Examples:
    red exdesc north You see a large tree to the north.

        the north to "You see a large tree to the north."  If in your
        main description, you hint that there is a large tree to the
        north, it might be a good idea to put an exdesc similar to
        this on the exit.

    red exdesc gate
        You can also specify named exits to describe with this command.
        In this case, you will be prompted for a description.  Looking
        at a gate, or door of any type, may provide clues to the key,
        or other pertinent information.  (e.g. You see a thick, bronze

room in that direction.  A player will not see that.

Creates an exit from one room to another.  Direction may be an actual
direction (n,s,e,w,nw,ne,sw,se,u,d) or a number.  Numbers are automatically
assigned to the normal directions.  If oexit is specified, the exit will be
one-way, in other words you can't get back the way you came.  Interesting
effects can be created with pairs of oexits leading to DIFFERENT rooms than
the way you came in.

Examples:
    red exit w 4000     [makes exit to room 4000 leading west]
    red oexit n 100     [makes one-way exit north to room 100]
    red exit 50 4000    [makes exit #50 lead to room 4000]

Note that numbered exits not expressly given names must be named with the
redit EXNAME (see red_exname) command.
Same as red_exit except its for one way exits. See red_exit for full info.

This command will set keywords for a door or exit without affecting other
fields of the exit (e.g. key, dflags, etc...)  Having a named exit is useful
if you want the exit to be a bit more descriptive than 'north' or 'up' such
as a gate, or an oak door.  Note that "red door" has a keyword field that
sets door keywords in the same manner.  Use the "red exname" if you only
want to change the keywords.

Examples:
    red exname down hole
        This will set the name for the exit 'down' to 'hole' instead.
        Where 'down' may be descriptive enough in most situations,
        seeing 'hole' will give players pause, and perhaps make them
        more inclined to skim through the room description for clues
        as to where the 'hole' takes them.

    red oexname north portal
        Changes the exit for the northern exit to 'portal'.  This may
        indicate some sort of one-way magical exit or hole in the wall,
                etc...  This will not change the reverse exit, if it exists.

As room descriptions should be more than just text displayed on entrance,
extras are things in the room that players can "look" at.  These should be
rather common in your descriptions.  If there is a chair in your description,
put an extra for it.  If there is a picture in your description, put an extra
for it.  If there is a big rock, put an extra for it.  The point of all this
is that players should be able to "look" at anything that's described in the
main description without getting the cryptic message "You don't see a <foo>
here."  You will be prompted to enter a description in the same way you
are for the main room description.
(Note: extras are deleted with redit delete)

Special extras:
You can define several "special" extras, which begin with an underscore (_)
which players will not be able to look at.  These are set up for special
purposes such as a teleport message (red extra _teleport) or a message which
is displayed when a player leaves through a particular exit (red extra _ex##,
where ## is the exit number and the exit is flagged "message".)

Examples:
    red extra oak tree  [Create and describe an extra with keywords
                 "oak" and "tree" (same description for both)]
    red extra _ex1      [Define the text seen when a player exits
                 through exit #1 (must have "message" flag set
                 for exit #1)]
    red extra _teleport [Define the message displayed when the room
                 teleport goes off]
